title: Invariance under extension of algebraically closed fields
statement:
Let $k\subseteq k'$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a
smooth separated curve
over $k$, and let $d\geq1$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$. For
every $q\geq0$ the pullback map

$$
H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)
$$

is an isomorphism.
(*The connected-curve input is [thm-sc-constant-invariance] of the Jacobian chapter. Stacks Tag 0A5B gives the smooth-curve route; Tag 0A5E states the corresponding result under properness.*)

proof.text: Fix $d\ge1$ invertible in $k$ and $q\ge0$, and write $\pi:C_{k\prime}\to C$ for the base-change projection. By def-sc-constant-sheaves, $\mathbf F_d$ means the constant abelian sheaf $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$, also when $d$ is composite; it does not mean a field of cardinality $d$. By def-sc-field-extension the comparison $\rho^q$ is the cohomology pullback along $\pi$. Use the natural constant-sheaf isomorphism $\pi^{-1}(\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)_C\cong(\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)_{C_{k\prime}}$ to normalize its target. Thus the comparison to be proved is exactly the displayed map, not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism between groups.

source.place: Proof, application of thm-sc-constant-invariance, with finite component reduction made explicit

proof.text: Apply the smooth curve/point decomposition to $C$: write it as a finite coproduct of smooth separated connected one-dimensional curves $D_i$ and copies $P_j=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its hypotheses hold because a curve here is separated and finite type of dimension at most one, and smoothness is assumed. Allow either or both families to be empty. All inclusions are open and closed.

For each $D_i$, use lem-sc-compactification to choose a smooth proper connected compactification with finite closed complement. Apply thm-sc-constant-invariance with $n=d$ and this compactification. Its hypotheses are exactly algebraic closure of both fields, connectedness, smoothness, separatedness, and $d\ge1$ prime to the characteristic. Its stated conclusion is bijectivity of the canonical $\rho^q$ for $D_i$ in every degree. Its extra proper/affine compatibility clauses are not needed. The notation and normalization of step 1 identify this with the required constant-coefficient comparison for $D_i$.

source.place: Proof, application of thm-sc-constant-invariance, with finite component reduction made explicit

proof.text: For each $P_j=\operatorname{Spec}k$, its base change is $\operatorname{Spec}k\prime$ with its unique point. The finite-geometric-point cohomology theorem with a singleton index set gives zero groups in positive degrees and identifies degree zero with the geometric stalk. The constant-stalk theorem identifies these stalks with $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$. In degree zero the map is the identity: a constant section with value $a$ pulls back to the constant section with value $a$, by the constant-pullback unit formula (composition of the constant function with the projection). Thus the canonical comparison is bijective in degree zero too; in positive degrees it is the unique map between zero groups.

source.place: Tag 03QU (lemma-compare-cohomology-point), with the singleton reduction of Tag 0A5B (lemma-constant-smooth-statements), first proof paragraph. The degree-zero constant-section calculation is the agent argument written in this step, using the canonical unit formula in lem-weil-pbc-constant-pullback-unit-continuous-map; it is not a statement of Tag 03Q1.

proof.text: Apply finite-coproduct cohomology assembly to the decomposition of $C$, and apply the finite-coproduct constant-base-change square to its structure morphism over $k$. For every summand $E_a$ the target coordinate of the comparison of $x$ equals the comparison of the restriction $x_a$. Each summand comparison is bijective by steps 3 and 4. If two classes have the same image, component injectivity gives equality of every restriction, and source assembly gives equality of the classes. Given a target class, take the preimage of each of its finitely many target coordinates by the corresponding component bijection, then use source assembly to obtain a class with those restrictions. The coordinate equation and injectivity of target assembly show that it maps to the given class. This proves bijectivity of the precise pullback. For an empty index set both products are the zero group and the same argument applies.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $k\subseteq k'$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a
smooth separated curve
over $k$, and let $d\geq1$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$. For
every $q\geq0$ the pullback map

$$
H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)
$$

is an isomorphism. Moreover, for $C$ proper and connected the computation
of [thm-sc-proper-cohomology] is compatible with this extension of the base
field: the isomorphisms recorded there over $k$ and over $k'$ are matched by
these pullback maps, not merely abstractly isomorphic.

proof.text:
A smooth separated curve over $k$ is a finite disjoint union of connected
components, each either a point (where both sides are the cohomology of a
separably closed field, and the map is an isomorphism) or a smooth separated
connected curve; cohomology takes the union to a product and the pullback map
respects it. For a connected curve the assertion is
[thm-sc-constant-invariance] of the Jacobian chapter (applied with $n=d$),
which proves it for the constant sheaf $\mathbf F_d$; this is the displayed
pullback map by the definition of the etale cohomology of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

*Compatibility in the proper case.* Let $C$ be proper and connected, of genus
$g$; then $C_{k'}$ has the same genus ([lem-sc-genus-invariant]), so
[thm-sc-proper-cohomology] gives $\mathbf Z/d$, $(\mathbf Z/d)^{2g}$,
$\mathbf Z/d$ on both sides. All maps below are canonical pullbacks, and the
Kummer sequence is natural in the base field. In degree $0$ the identification
is $\mu_d(k)=\mu_d(k')$: a primitive $d$-th root of unity of $k$ stays primitive
in $k'$ ([lem-sc-primitive-root]). In degree $1$ it is
$H^1(C,\mu_d)=\operatorname{Pic}(C)[d]$ ([lem-sc-kummer-les]; the units of $C$
are the $d$-divisible group $k^\times$) together with
$\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)=J_C(k)$ ([thm-sc-jacobian-representability]); the
pullback is $J_C[d](k)\to J_C[d](k')$, which is bijective because $J_C[d]$ is a
finite etale $k$-group scheme ([thm-av-final](b),(c)) and
$J_{C_{k'}}=(J_C)_{k'}$ ([thm-sc-jacobian-representability]). In degree $2$ it
is $\operatorname{Pic}(C)/d\to\operatorname{Pic}(C_{k'})/d$, where both sides
are $\mathbf Z/d$ via the degree ([def-sc-pic0],
[lem-sc-pic-proper-decomposition]), and the degree is preserved by base
change. So the three identifications are matched by the pullback maps.
